period.caveat: Quick sinusoid-grid estimate (per-detector amplitude and phase, per-wavelength-bin offsets). The best grid period of pure noise is still a number: read it only when 'significant' (visit-permutation false-alarm probability <= 1 %). Seasonal gaps make aliases (see the other peaks), real light curves are not sinusoids and the formal error ignores model error: confirm with an independent contemporaneous light curve and catalog periods before quoting it.

notes: 450 of 538 exposures in the light curve (wing method, 111 wavelength bins of 1.0% per detector, bins spanning >= 30 d).
Relative magnitudes: each point against the mean magnitude of its own detector and wavelength bin; the same detector does not mean the same wavelength (linear variable filter).
Wing photometry (12-20 px minus 40-55 px, MJy/sr): RELATIVE brightness only; 538 exposures have a saturated core.
Control: 6 comparison stars measured with the aperture method in the same exposures; robust scatter (mag) D1 0.016, D2 0.022, D3 0.024, D4 0.032, D5 0.083, D6 0.117.
Period 259.1 d: significant (visit-permutation false-alarm probability 0.010, 100 permutations); quick sinusoid estimate, check the aliases and the caveat.
Offline FITS measurement using WS3 variability methods; not a new R05 validation.
Fixed sky position. This calculation does not follow proper motion or parallax.
Aperture flux is uncorrected aperture flux; wing flux is relative surface brightness only.
Relative magnitudes are normalized per detector/wavelength bin; negative means brighter.
zero_point_mag is reported but not applied; rel_mag_err is statistical, read comparison controls for systematics.
A truncated selection may alter a period estimate. Inspect significance, aliases and independent data.
